headline: High risk of filesystem conflict and cascading misuse: shared workspace plus write access make Continue→Plandex interactions dangerous by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Continue can read workspace files and use MCP, while Plandex reads and writes the project directory plus plan-local sandbox. That creates a shared-file bridge where attacker-controlled content in files can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks explicit provenance tracking or isolation in the profiles, so the interaction is plausible in default coding workflows.
conditions: IF Continue ingests workspace files as instructions without provenance checks
IF Plandex writes attacker-controlled text into the shared project directory
mitigations: Restrict both agents to separate directories for prompts and outputs
Require manual review of any file-derived instructions before execution
Disable MCP tools for untrusted repositories
Add a provenance header to generated files
requires-engineering: implement content-sanitization and instruction/data separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Continue touches open editor buffers and workspace files, and Plandex accesses the project directory and plan-local sandbox. Because both can read the same code workspace, sensitive source or buffer contents can flow between them through shared files. Neither profile shows default encryption, access partitioning, or local-only guarantees that would block this.
conditions: IF the shared workspace contains secrets or proprietary source
IF either agent copies file contents into outputs or logs
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared project directory
Use separate workspaces per agent
Redact sensitive files before opening them in either tool
Turn off automatic file import/export features
requires-engineering: add workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Continue has write_filesystem and shared_state via filesystem, while Plandex has write_filesystem, execute_shell, modify_git_state, and shared_state via Plandex server backend. In a shared repo, both can mutate the same files and git state, and the profiles show no locking or coordination primitive. That makes concurrent edits and state corruption dangerous by default.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository path
IF Plandex auto-applies changes while Continue is editing the same files
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate checkout
Disable auto-apply in Plandex
Serialize edits through one operator-controlled queue
Use git branches per agent
requires-engineering: add file-locking or merge arbitration

D_cascading_error.rationale: Continue can produce code edits from MCP-driven tool use, and Plandex is a multi-step planner with review-then-apply or optional auto-apply. If Plandex treats Continue's output as authoritative, an error can cascade into committed or applied changes. The profiles do not show a verification gate between them, so the blast radius includes incorrect code changes.
conditions: IF Plandex consumes Continue-generated patches or explanations without independent verification
IF auto-apply is enabled in Plandex
mitigations: Require human review before apply
Ask Plandex to re-derive critical changes from source files
Disable auto-apply
Compare diffs against a second tool before commit
requires-engineering: add structured verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source coding tools that touch source code and editor/project files, so there is no documented residency or regulated-data mismatch in the profiles. Continue handles model-provider API keys and Plandex handles model-provider API keys, but the pairwise compliance risk is limited to ordinary code-workspace handling rather than a specific policy breach.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into the shared code workspace
IF an operator routes sensitive files through either agent
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the coding workspace
Use separate tenants or accounts for any hosted model providers
Review retention settings for connected model providers
Document data-handling boundaries for the pair
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated files
